# Election update: Tuesday, November 17 (morning)

## Bottom line
Democrats flipped Tennessee's 4th District, a seat every forecaster rated Solid R: Rep. Scott DesJarlais (R) conceded to Victoria Broderick (D) after Nashville counted its provisional ballots, Tennessee Lookout reports ([Tennessee Lookout](https://tennesseelookout.com/2026/11/16/desjarlais-concedes-tennessee-4th-congressional-district-to-democrat-victoria-broderick/)). The House results table now marks 432 of 435 races called: D 260, R 172, with 218 needed for a majority ([House table](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_House_of_Representatives_elections)). The Senate stands at D 55, R 44, counting seats not up, with Alaska the last race outstanding ([Senate table](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_Senate_elections)). Governorships are final at D 30, R 20 of 50, counting the 14 states with no race this year, with six flips, all to Democrats ([governor table](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_gubernatorial_elections)). Eight seats rated safe came in within 5 points: Democrats flipped TN-04, and Republicans held the other seven (six in the results table, plus CA-23 per [NBC News](https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2026-elections/california-us-house-district-23-results); TN-04 per [NBC News](https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2026-elections/tennessee-us-house-district-4-results)).

## Called since the last update
- **Flip (1, D): HOU-TN-04 (rated safe).** Broderick defeated eight-term Rep. DesJarlais, who conceded Monday afternoon ([Tennessee Lookout](https://tennesseelookout.com/2026/11/16/desjarlais-concedes-tennessee-4th-congressional-district-to-democrat-victoria-broderick/)). The results table marks it a Democratic gain ([House table](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_House_of_Representatives_elections)).
- **Hold (1, R): HOU-NC-07** (Likely R). Kimberly Hardy (D) conceded to Rep. David Rouzer (R), WHQR reports ([WHQR](https://news.google.?oc=5)).
- **Hold (1, R): HOU-CA-23 (rated safe).** Rep. Jay Obernolte (R) is marked re-elected over Tessa Hodge (D) in the results table ([House table](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_House_of_Representatives_elections)).
- **Rated safe, came in close:** the table's updated Florida counts show three more Solid R seats held by Republicans within 5 points: FL-26 (Rep. Mario Díaz-Balart, by 0.8 points), FL-18 (Rep. Scott Franklin, by 3.6), and FL-02 (Austin Rogers, by 4.2) ([House table](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_House_of_Representatives_elections)).

## Still uncalled
Every race still outstanding, Senate first, then House.
- **SEN-AK** (Tossup): in the state's count of Nov. 16, 5:13 p.m., Mary Peltola (D) has 141,637 first-choice votes (49.98%) to 130,162 (45.93%) for Sen. Dan S. Sullivan (R). She is 52 votes short of a first-choice majority, which would decide the race without ranked-choice rounds ([Alaska Division of Elections](https://www.elections.alaska.gov/enr/26GENR/results/ElectionSummaryReportRPT.pdf)). She took 55.9% of the 1,790 votes added in that count. The final count of absentee and questioned ballots, and ranked-choice results if needed, come Wednesday, Nov. 18. Newsweek reports Sullivan has broken his silence on the race ([Newsweek](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMinwFBVV95cUxQQlY2Q1dTdjdLR1gtZjhIOWxhbTBkSFV0R0dER3lFVjFSQm5BdUpMYmQyUUhSdjFJVURkNWlzZHFTcUluQkZJdWFneE1JeGJ4dDJYTFJaTndPWTNETHA1U3BtcnpCV0lYaVdHWk1CVllOQkJfRndESS1zeUR4M2RJQ0xPYXVaM2tWRkpOdmpQblVRWEJOblRwSTJqVlRGZE0?oc=5)).
- **HOU-AK-AL** (Lean R): Rep. Nick Begich (R) has 47.67% of first-choice votes to 41.70% for Bill Hill (nonpartisan) and 7.84% for Eric Hafner (D). That is 6,572 votes short of a majority, so the race goes to ranked-choice tabulation on Wednesday ([Alaska Division of Elections](https://www.elections.alaska.gov/enr/26GENR/results/ElectionSummaryReportRPT.pdf)).
- **HOU-NC-05** (Likely R): Rep. Virginia Foxx (R) has requested a recount in her race against Chuck Hubbard (D), WXII reports ([WXII](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMitAFBVV95cUxNdGdLa0QzT1ZWaWdLVmJTZ0lCYkp6WFExT1djS3JUY09FYnpRbXpqb1FjSkdxanVnV2hWVEJSekpBRzg5UWtSaGlUQ0lMXzdEdUhKMzltSld3QmpwQlFIUHhValQ5OXYxYXNWQkwwTnhwdXF3cTRQcWM3dW4yVDRYbzhxSjFOaHdYSGFQemtnNG4zNDgxMFdla3BvRlF1SGZTWW55eGlGN3ZWUXB0Z0ljUnBxSWc?oc=5)).
- **HOU-MN-01** (Lean R): Jake Johnson (D) leads Rep. Brad Finstad (R) by 322 votes, per the Secretary of State as reported Sunday by KTTC ([KTTC](https://www.kttc.com/2026/11/16/lead-rochester-data-center-hundred-million-dollar-deficits-olmsted-county-priorities-election-recounts/)). A publicly funded recount is likely, WIZM reports ([WIZM](https://news.google.?oc=5)).

## Recounts and certification
- **North Carolina:** recounts are scheduled this week in congressional and legislative races, WUNC reports ([WUNC](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMitwFBVV95cUxPXy1qZVJWSlR5dXRLbHRWNFJ1a2tKS0N4N3VDQnZ0QVhOa1FVRVZJSU9QOV9lSHdkNE9ndVlSVHRNalpNY3JaeUNxZE5VRjJZWnpndVVhcmZTckxTWVUxMnhGMVRGcUp1aS1rbTdia2Yxdm40cmZQWFYxVTVrbGl5V3F6SDY2dFFnU19DNmFUbHdfbmRvUG9HTXBfVGNzeVhNM3I0aVo3R0ViNkk5VUNYai1iT1o1OTQ?oc=5)).
- **Minnesota:** the State Canvassing Board certifies results Thursday, Nov. 19, which starts the window to request a recount ([KTTC](https://news.google.?oc=5)).
- **Alaska:** certification is slated for Nov. 25, Alaska Public Media reported ([Alaska Public Media](https://alaskapublic.org/news/politics/elections/2026-11-13/peltola-leads-in-u-s-senate-race-nearing-50-mark-with-almost-all-ballots-counted)).

## Legal and federal action
- **Indiana:** a judge blocked state Senate leader Chris Garten (R) from starting his new term after a Democratic lawsuit, WTHR reports ([WTHR](https://news.google.?oc=5)).
- **Federal dockets:** CourtListener shows filings in 26 election-related federal dockets since Nov. 14, none bearing on an uncalled race ([CourtListener](https://www.courtlistener.com/docket/75028945/potter-county-republican-party-v-benge/)).

## What voters said
- **Infrequent voters:** an analysis found Democratic enthusiasm among less-frequent voters in Texas and Georgia, ABC News reports ([ABC News](https://news.google.?oc=5)).
- **Trump voters who stayed home:** Newsmax (right-leaning) reports a poll finding 35% of Trump voters skipped the midterms ([Newsmax](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMihwFBVV95cUxOWU14bWdDUXhsRWhUc2FRSENmazFHZDBnZXlYNFBrcEVUZGJpaUY2bl9BQkRXTERZQ00xOHFzcjFqaGw5V0hrSGFUWDVUYVJpUTdJYUhUOEQ4cXktWEgyREdDTVMyMjBQTnJQa1J3WmxJTlZzQTBlbEt4LTFKRGZ0bkNWNEt6N0k?oc=5)). No new voter-file read from Ralston or Bitzer is in today's leads.

## Coverage note
- **Parser:** the House (435 rows) and Senate (35) tables parsed and the health check is clean. Alaska figures come from the state's own report, read this morning.
- **Digest gap:** the digest listed TN-04 as a safe seat "called as rated," but the winner flipped the seat. It is reported here as a flip; the digest check needs a fix in an attended session.
- **Court records:** CourtListener used (3 requests; 26 election dockets).
- **Lessons learned:** returns next Monday.
